questions.title: Question 1: The Account tester (12 marks)
questions.prompt: Finish the lecture's `Account` class with `deposit(amount)`, `withdraw(amount)` and `transferFunds(to, amount)` (transfer only if the first account has enough). Create 21347 with P38763.87 and 61342 with P0.00, deposit P500.00 into the second, withdraw P1000.00 from the first, and then transfer P500.00 from the first to the second. Give both balances and say what `transferFunds(second, 9999.00)` does afterwards. (12 marks)

steps.title: The methods
steps.body: `deposit` adds the amount to the balance, `withdraw` subtracts it, and `transferFunds(Account to, double amount)` is `if (balance >= amount) { withdraw(amount); to.deposit(amount); }`. (4 marks)

steps.title: The tester
steps.body: After the deposit the second balance is 500.00. After the withdrawal the first is 37763.87. After the transfer the first is 37263.87 and the second is 1000.00. (5 marks)

steps.title: The failed transfer
steps.body: `transferFunds(second, 9999.00)` does nothing when the first balance is smaller than the amount: neither `withdraw` nor `deposit` is called, so both balances stay as they were. (3 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** 37263.87 and 1000.00; an unaffordable transfer changes nothing.

questions.title: Question 2: Valid or not valid? (12 marks)
questions.prompt: With `Rectangle` and `Circle` extending `Shape`, classify: (a) `Shape s1 = new Shape();` (b) `Shape s3 = new Rectangle();` (c) `s3.setColour("Orange");` (d) `Rectangle s4 = new Shape();` (e) `Systems.out.println(s1.toString());` (f) `Circle c = (Circle) s3;` (g) `Shape s5 = new Circle("Yellow");` when `Circle` has only `Circle()` and `Circle(int)`. Give the compiler message or run-time result for those that fail. (12 marks)

steps.title: Valid statements
steps.body: (a), (b) and (c) are valid: a `Rectangle` is a `Shape`, and `setColour` is inherited. (3 marks)

steps.title: Compile errors
steps.body: (d) `incompatible types: Shape cannot be converted to Rectangle`. (e) `package Systems does not exist`. (g) `incompatible types: String cannot be converted to int`, because there is no `Circle(String)` constructor. (6 marks)

steps.title: The cast
steps.body: (f) compiles, because `Shape` and `Circle` are related, but `s3` holds a `Rectangle`, so it throws `ClassCastException` at run time. (3 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** (a), (b), (c) valid; (d), (e), (g) do not compile; (f) fails at run time.

questions.title: Question 3: What a sub class can and cannot do (10 marks)
questions.prompt: (a) State what a sub class can do and cannot do. (b) `Circle extends Shape` returns `colour + " circle"` from `toString`, and `colour` is private in `Shape`. Give the compiler message and two repairs. (c) A sub class constructor has no `super(...)` and `Base` has only `Base(String c)`. Give the message and the repair. (10 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: Can: inherit public fields and methods, add instance variables and methods, override methods. Cannot: remove super class members, inherit private members, inherit constructors. (4 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: `error: colour has private access in Shape`. Repairs: use the public getter `getColour()`, or make the variable `protected`. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: `error: constructor Base in class Base cannot be applied to given types` (required String, found no arguments), because the compiler inserts `super()`. Repair: `super("text");` as the first statement. (3 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** Private members are not inherited; a sub class constructor must call a super class constructor that exists.

questions.title: Question 4: Overriding, partial overriding and equals (14 marks)
questions.prompt: (a) Give the rules for overriding. (b) Explain why `String toString()` without `public` in a sub class does not compile. (c) Explain why `super.toString();` on its own line has no effect. (d) Shape has `equals(Shape)`; a sub class adds `equals(Object)`. For a red circle and a red rectangle, what does `redCircle.equals(redRect)` give, and why? Give a version that works. (14 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: The classes are connected by inheritance (is-a); the two methods have the same name, return type and signature; `@Override` asks the compiler to check that there is a method to override. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: `toString()` in `Object` is public and an overriding method may not have weaker access: `attempting to assign weaker access privileges; was public`. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: `super.toString()` returns a String; as a statement on its own the value is discarded. Use it: `return super.toString() + " with radius = " + radius;`. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (d)
steps.body: It gives `true`, which is wrong: the compiler chooses the most specific method for the argument type, `Shape.equals(Shape)`, which compares colours only. A version that works has one `equals(Object)` in the base class (same object, `null` or `getClass()` different, then cast and compare) and the sub classes call `super.equals(o)` before comparing their own variables. (5 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** `true` (wrong) with the overload present; with a single `equals(Object)` all the way up the hierarchy the answer is `false`.

questions.title: Question 5: Abstract classes and interfaces (12 marks)
questions.prompt: (a) Define an abstract class and an interface and give the error for `new Shape()` when `Shape` is abstract. (b) Give the compiler messages for: a concrete `Circle` that does not implement `getArea()`; `void methodA() { }` implementing an interface method; `class Two extends A, B`. (c) Explain why a class can implement several interfaces but extend only one class. (12 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: An abstract class is declared with `abstract`, may have abstract methods (no body), cannot be instantiated and is extended by a concrete class; an interface is a collection of public abstract method signatures (and constants), with no constructor, implemented with `implements`. `new Shape()`: `Shape is abstract; cannot be instantiated`. (4 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: `Circle is not abstract and does not override abstract method getArea() in Shape`; `methodA() in Bob cannot implement methodA() in Test` (weaker access privileges; was public); `'{' expected`. (5 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: An interface holds only method signatures, with no data, so several can be combined without conflict; this is how Java enables multiple inheritance. A class holds data and code, so Java allows one super class. (3 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** Abstract classes and interfaces cannot be instantiated; implement every abstract method with public access.

questions.title: Question 6: Lab 5, the doctors (14 marks)
questions.prompt: A `Doctor` has a last name, a first name and a basic pay. A `GP` adds an allowance rate (a percentage of basic pay) and a `Surgeon` adds a number of procedures and a rate per procedure. Give the tag and monthly pay for GP Dube, first name Neo, basic pay 28000, rate 10, and for Surgeon Moeng, first name Kagiso, basic pay 40000, 6 procedures at 500. Say how `data.txt` lines are told apart. (14 marks)

steps.title: The GP
steps.body: `tagName()` calls `super.tagName()` (`Dr. Dube N.`) and adds ` (GP)`: `Dr. Dube N. (GP)`. `calculatePay()` is basic pay plus the allowance: 28000 + 28000 x 10 / 100 = 30800.00. (5 marks)

steps.title: The Surgeon
steps.body: `Dr. Moeng K. (Surgeon)`. The pay is the basic pay plus procedures times rate: 40000 + 6 x 500 = 43000.00 (the sheet's paragraph gives this formula; its bullet, "return the doctor's monthly pay", contradicts it). (5 marks)

steps.title: The data file
steps.body: After splitting each line at the semicolons: three items is a plain `Doctor`, four (a rate) is a `GP`, five (rate and procedures) is a `Surgeon`. The tester writes each tag and pay to `doctors.txt`, `gps.txt` or `surgeons.txt` by type (`instanceof`). (4 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** `Dr. Dube N. (GP) 30800.00` and `Dr. Moeng K. (Surgeon) 43000.00`.

questions.title: Question 7: Lab 6, the payroll (14 marks)
questions.prompt: Describe the Lab 6 question 1 classes and program: the abstract `Employee` (name, ID, overloaded constructors, abstract `computeSalary()`, `toString`, `equals`), `Teacher` (subject, hours, hourly rate) and `Admin` (monthly salary, role), and `RunPayroll`. Give the salary of Teacher Tom (120 hours at 95.67) and Admin Mary (4000), say how a record is recognised, and say why `new Employee("Tom")` fails. (14 marks)

steps.title: The classes
steps.body: `Employee` is abstract because `computeSalary()` has no body. `Teacher.computeSalary()` returns hours times hourly rate; `Admin.computeSalary()` returns the monthly salary. `equals` in `Teacher` compares subject, ID and salary, and in `Admin` role, ID and salary. (5 marks)

steps.title: RunPayroll
steps.body: A record with four items is an `Admin`, one with five is a `Teacher`. Each is stored in an `Employee` array; `computeSalary()` runs the method of each object's own class (polymorphism); the payments and a total go to `teacherspay.txt` and `adminpay.txt`, and the totals and the wage bill are displayed. `new Employee("Tom")` fails: `Employee is abstract; cannot be instantiated`. (6 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** Tom 11480.40 and Mary 4000.00; the abstract class cannot be instantiated.
